slug: 2026-02-27 Who Protects Nigeria's Digital Citizens Unmasking Accountability Gaps in Digital Rights Governance

facts.fact: On 5 June 2021 the Nigerian government announced an indefinite suspension of Twitter after it deleted posts by the then president, and telecom providers were directed to block it nationwide; the document says it lasted over seven months.

Department of State Services operatives arrested Ambrose Nwaogwugwu, a Peoples Democratic Party social media manager in Imo State, over a satirical online post about the state governor; he was charged with defamation and false publication and held several weeks before bail.
Lagos authorities detained activist Abdulganiu Olushipo briefly on allegations of cyberstalking after he publicly questioned a local government budget.

Military personnel detained Segun Olatunji, editor of FirstNews, on 15 March 2024 after he published a report alleging financial misconduct by a senior government official; he was held 14 days in Abuja.
Reporters Without Borders reported in 2024 that at least eight journalists had been arrested, prosecuted or detained under the Cybercrimes Act despite its amendment.
Lagos nurse Olamide Thomas was arrested in December 2024 after livestreaming remarks critical of President Tinubu and senior officials, charged with cyberbullying and detained until bail days later.

Amnesty International and other civil society and human rights organisations criticised the 2019 draft hate-speech and internet falsehoods bills as restrictions on freedom of expression, and the provisions were revised.

facts.fact: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria filed complaints in 2021 that the mandate to link SIM cards to a National Identification Number lets the state identify and spy on internet users.
